patch.value: GH-1715: pm history-repair rewrites recorded entries after a mid-chain break, so the only drift remedy breaks append-only consumers and later merges

GH-1715 (filed 2026-11-12). When an item history chain breaks mid-stream (an unrecorded change landed between two recorded entries, such as a hand edit or a merge resolution that bypassed pm), pm history-repair re-anchors the chain by rewriting every recorded entry after the break (before_hash, after_hash and record_hash recomputed as if the unrecorded change had not happened) and appends one history_repair entry at repair time. Three problems follow. First, bytes other writers already hold change, so a later merge of two clones of the history file conflicts or duplicates entries and breaks the chain again. Second, an append-only consumer check (main's bytes are a prefix of the branch's bytes) must refuse the repair: in the fleet, one package's release gate refuses it with history_prefix_replaced, so the only remedy pm health offers for history_drift_chain_mismatch keeps that package's scheduled strict-health closeout red. Third, the rewritten entries misstate the order, claiming the unrecorded change happened after them although pm health knew where the break was. Proposal from the issue: an append-only repair, by default or behind --append-only, that appends one audited bridge record naming the break (the first entry whose before_hash does not match) and the reconciled on-disk state, leaves every earlier line byte-identical, and makes chain verification accept the bridge.

pm history-repair offers an append-only repair that appends one audited bridge record naming the break and leaves every earlier line byte-identical; History chain verification and pm health accept a bridged stream, and a merge of two clones of a bridged stream stays verifiable; The bridge records where the unrecorded change happened instead of claiming it happened at repair time
The drift remedy appends a bridge record and never rewrites recorded entries
history-repair recomputes the hashes of every entry after the break

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Design as implemented, 2026-11-21. One sealed history_repair record carries bridge {version: 1, breaks: [{gap_from, gap_to, record_hash}]}. gap_from is the after_hash recorded before the break, gap_to the before_hash recorded after it, and record_hash belongs to the break entry (null for a legacy entry). Its patch is jsonPatch.compare(replay without the unrecorded change, on-disk item). Its before_hash is the last recorded after_hash, and its after_hash is the on-disk item hash, so replay re-anchors on the truth at the bridge.

Verifier (verifyHistoryChainWithVersion, src/core/history/replay.ts): an anchored before-hash mismatch opens a segment only when the next bridge's first descriptor names exactly that break. Inside the segment each patch must still apply strictly, and each recorded link must hold or be the next named break. At the bridge, every named break must have occurred, its before_hash must link, and replay plus its patch must hash to its after_hash. Failures: bridge_invalid (malformed, unsealed or non-history_repair, pre-scanned so it wins over an earlier break), bridge_unnamed_break, bridge_names_absent_break, bridge_link_mismatch, bridge_after_hash_mismatch, bridge_without_break. The result adds bridged_segments. DRIFT_CACHE_VERSION 11 -> 12 so an older pm never trusts a verdict computed under these semantics.

Repair (src/sdk/history/append-only-repair.ts): name the first replay mismatch plus every later recorded-link mismatch, build the record, and require the extended stream to verify before writing. The write appends to the exact bytes read under the lock and refuses non-UTF-8 streams. Refusal: history_append_only_repair_unavailable with reason chain_failure_not_a_break, patch_does_not_replay, item_missing, stream_not_utf8 or bridge_does_not_verify; next step is the rewriting repair. The pm health remedy for history_drift_chain_mismatch now names --append-only. --all passes through.

Rewrite interaction: reanchorHistoryEntries keeps a verified bridged segment byte-identical while nothing before it changed, so the rewriting repair is a no-op on a bridged stream. A rewrite before the segment, or any projected rewrite (merge union), dissolves the bridge into an ordinary record and keeps the original sealed record as rewrite evidence (retainPriorRecord), so a stale bridge never survives. Merge: two clones that bridged the same break (identical bridge, patch, anchors, version and algorithm) merge as equivalent_bridges. Ours stays byte-for-byte and theirs is appended as a neutral record with an empty patch and the original in evidence, so both repairs keep their provenance.

Known limit: versions between a break and its bridge lack the unrecorded change, so restore and get --at refuse them with history_replay_invalid. Versions before the break and from the bridge onward stay addressable. Cross-version: an older pm reports drift on a bridged stream, and its rewriting repair keeps the unknown bridge field. This pm then reports bridge_without_break, and its own rewriting repair dissolves the bridge.

value.text:
Review round 1 on PR #1762 (Codex gpt-6.2-sol xhigh, 13 findings; Greptile, 3 findings that overlap Codex). Every finding was accepted and fixed in the second commit.

Bridge integrity: the bridge envelope gains segment_digest, a digest under the record's algorithm of every record from the first break up to the bridge. Previously only the break entries were named, so an interior record with its seal stripped and its patch changed still verified whenever a later patch overwrote the changed value. Inside a segment, any entry whose recorded before-state replay proves (for example after a recorded change overwrote the edited field) must also match its recorded after-state. New failure code: bridge_segment_mismatch.

Dissolution: a union merge, a rewrite before the segment, or history-redact must re-anchor a bridged segment on replay that lacks the unrecorded change. Each now marks the covered entries with the sealed field replay_inexact and keeps the original bridge as rewrite evidence. Redaction used to refuse every bridged stream with bridge_without_break; it now dissolves the bridge and verifies. replayHistoryToTarget (restore and get --at) refuses such versions with the new code history_version_unreconstructable, and refuses versions inside a verified open segment the same way (previously history_replay_invalid).

Repair: the bridge anchors on the epoch the verified prefix proves instead of the rewrite resolver's epoch-1 fallback for implicit streams. Reconciliation reuses the tail's epoch-2 variant. The preview reports reconciliation and the history_repair_reconcile_discards_events warning, like the rewriting repair. The append refuses with the new reason stream_changed when the bytes read for the write differ from the verified snapshot.

Merge: equivalent_bridges now requires both sides and the result to verify, and appends to ours' raw bytes (CRLF-safe). Salvage parses trimmed lines like the shared reader (BOM).

Package: the import-closure check moved from package-artifact-gate into package-distribution's leased staging. It runs on the exact staged bytes and lexes with TypeScript preProcessFile, so comments and template text are not edges and from /* comment */ "x" is. A negative control without the graph.js exclusion refuses the pack.

Regression tests: tests/integration/lifecycle/history-bridge.integration.spec.ts (17 tests), tests/unit/sdk/history/append-only-repair.spec.ts (epoch-2 implicit prefix, field-frozen variant, stream_changed and UTF-8 guards), tests/unit/scripts/package-distribution.spec.ts (lexer controls plus a real refused pack).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Review round 2 on PR #1762: Codex (9 findings) and CodeRabbit (5 findings on the round-1 head). All were accepted and fixed in the third commit.

Root cause shared by most of them: knowledge that a bridged segment's versions cannot be reconstructed was only computed from a fully verified stream at rewrite time. Rewrites that reseal, interleave or repair records first could therefore dissolve a bridge without marking its versions. Fixed at one point: locateBridgedSegments (src/core/history/bridge.ts) finds each bridge's segment from its own commitments, its first named break plus its segment digest, without needing the stream before it to verify. Markers only restrict reads, so a forged bridge cannot widen what verifies. materializeBridgedSegments writes replay_inexact onto covered records before a rewrite can void the bridge. Users: provenance normalization (before resealing), merge unions (records a bridge covers on either original branch, matched by union identity, before interleaving), reanchor (a bridge dissolved because an earlier record was repaired) and redaction. history-redact now refuses a stream whose bridge does not locate its segment (history_redact_bridge_unlocated) instead of dropping that bridge's evidence. A compaction checkpoint at an inexact version inherits the marker.

Verifier: every record from the break to the bridge must be complete (record_incomplete); link-only checks are not enough for a record without a patch array. A declared epoch inside a segment, including on the break entry, now governs the unversioned records after it.

Repair: the record anchors on the newest declared epoch, otherwise the epoch the verified prefix proves. Its epoch-2 variant must be proven by replay or by the on-disk item, else it refuses with hash_surface_ambiguous. The write uses O_APPEND on the handle whose bytes were checked, syncs, and refuses stream_changed when the path no longer names that inode, so it never replaces bytes another writer added. The UTF-8 check also runs before planning, so dry-run and apply agree.

Merge identity now includes a record's bridge, so differing bridges never count as one shared record (an invalid bridge on one side can no longer make the merge identical). health keeps --append-only in the bulk remedy for history_drift_chain_mismatch. Import closure now uses a TypeScript AST walk (regex-literal control). TypeScript resolves from the packed checkout first and then from the script, so release controls copied without node_modules still pack.

Coverage: 212 related spec files (4,361 tests) pass with no uncovered changed line in the touched modules. The first hosted coverage run had found 4 gaps (since fixed), including item-revision.ts line 361: the decoder now refuses a null line before that catch, so its spec now uses a record without a patch array to keep exercising the catch.

value.text:
Review round 3 on PR #1762 (Codex, 7 findings) plus two hosted CI failures on the round-1 head. All were accepted and fixed in the fourth commit.

Replay mutated recorded patches: normalizeReplayPatchOps shared op values with the replay document, so a later op of the same patch changed the recorded value before the segment digest was computed. It now deep-copies values, so an unsealed record's original value can no longer be changed under a sealed bridge.

Unlocatable bridges: locateBridgedSegments now finds a segment by its first break plus digest, then by that break's recorded anchors (which survive the resealing that marking applies), and otherwise yields the conservative range from the record after the previous bridge. A rewrite therefore never serves an unlocatable bridge's versions as exact, at the cost of over-restricting.

Merges: every merge path, including identical and fast-forward results and equivalent bridges, keeps a replay_inexact marker that either branch already carries. Only the union path, which dissolves bridges, also marks each branch's bridge coverage, matched by union identity. Paths that keep live bridges never mark their segments (that would void the digests). A projected reanchor leaves marking to the merge driver.

Epochs: for an implicit stream, the appended record keeps the epoch the verified prefix proves unless the tail's own anchor proves only other epochs; it then takes the newest of those, and refuses hash_surface_ambiguous when nothing proves one. The verifier requires the bridge record to keep the epoch the stream declared (bridge_epoch_mismatch). Covered records must carry anchors that are well-formed digests of their algorithm (record_incomplete).

Concurrent same-inode writer: after the O_APPEND write, the repair re-reads the handle and reports stream_changed when the bytes are not exactly the verified prefix plus its record. It never rolls back peer bytes.

Packaging: hosted CI failed registry-acceptance-workflow, because the preserved release controls run in a foreign workspace without node_modules and the TypeScript lexer could not load. The import-closure check is now dependency-free. Under the build lease, listExcludedModules lists the modules the checkout holds under shipped module directories that the files list leaves out, and findExcludedModuleReferences refuses any staged module containing a quoted relative path that resolves to one of them. Every spelling counts (static, dynamic, require, worker URLs), and it fails closed for comments that name an excluded path.

value.text:
Review round 4 on PR #1762: Codex with gpt-6.2-astra after gpt-6.2-sol twice stopped at a content filter. 16 findings: 13 fixed, 3 deferred to pm-vtg2d8.

Fixed:
- Location grades. locateBridgedSegments marks a segment exact only when its digest matches from a start that the first break's record hash or anchors name; the record before the break may be damaged. A break-anchor start is otherwise accepted only when every covered record already carries replay_inexact (a rewrite marked it from an exact location). Anything else is unproven: it marks the conservative range since the previous bridge plus the bridge record itself. A later matching anchor pair can no longer shorten a segment.
- history-redact dissolves only exact segments and refuses otherwise. It rewrites the live item from replay, so a damaged segment must not authorize that.
- reanchorHistoryEntries derives coverage itself for projected rewrites too. Only a caller that declares callerMarksBridgeCoverage, as the merge driver does, skips it.
- Unions mark by merged position: every event placed between a branch segment's first covered record and its bridge.
- A neutralized bridge matches its original record's identity on later merges, so there are no duplicate repair records.
- Identical, fast-forward and equivalent results never mark records that a retained exact live bridge covers.
- An effect-free patch (empty or test-only) cannot be bridged with differing anchors.
- A repair that only dissolves a stray bridge or adds markers is persisted (ReanchorResult.entriesResealed).
- An unsupported tail digest is a typed refusal.
- The checked append opens with O_RDWR|O_APPEND and never creates the path; ENOENT becomes stream_changed.
- The closure check resolves extensionless, directory-index and query or fragment specifiers.
- The docs no longer claim a rewriting repair keeps a bridged segment byte-identical: it keeps the records, while only --append-only keeps the bytes.

Deferred to pm-vtg2d8, none of which loses data or serves a restore: before-values shown by history diffs, epoch-2 variant selection with duplicate replay matches, and holding the closer to a proven variant.

value.text: Review round 5 on PR #1762. Two full-diff Codex runs (gpt-6.2-astra) stopped at a content filter. A narrower gpt-6.2-sol review of the latest fix commits found 4 regressions they introduced, all fixed in the next commit. (1) Merge marking keyed merged positions by identity, so repeated identical events (same author, timestamp and patch) marked only the last copy. It now maps the k-th occurrence on a branch to the k-th occurrence in the merged stream. (2) Neutral bridge copies aliased to their original's identity created opposite ordering edges when two reciprocal equivalent-bridge merges were merged again. The equivalent-bridges path now accepts any suffixes made only of the same repair, live or neutral: ours is kept and only theirs' repairs ours does not represent are appended, so no ordering is needed. (3) entriesResealed counted epoch-label-only changes, so a clean mixed-era stream was rewritten by a rewriting repair. It now counts only bridge dissolution and new replay_inexact markers. (4) The package check stripped "#" before judging a specifier, while require() reads it literally; both spellings are now checked. Remaining finding classes are tracked on pm-vtg2d8.

It also asserts that restore refuses every covered version with history_version_unreconstructable before and after redaction, normalization, compaction and merge unions dissolve the bridge.

patch.value: The GH-1715 reproduction leaves the original four lines a byte prefix of the repaired file, pm health --strict-exit passes, and repeating either repair is a no-op. 30 integration cases cover forged and partial bridges, merges, redaction, normalization and compaction; the full touched-module suite (213 files, 4,375 tests) passes with no uncovered changed line.

pm history-repair --append-only (SDK and MCP appendOnly) appends one sealed history_repair record. Its bridge names every chain break by gap_from, gap_to and the break record hash, commits to the covered records with segment_digest, and reconciles replay with the on-disk item, so every earlier line stays byte-identical. The record is written with O_APPEND to the verified bytes. verifyHistoryChainWithVersion accepts a break only when the next bridge names it, checks recorded links, complete records and effects wherever replay realigns, and requires the bridge to keep the declared epoch and re-anchor replay. Rewrites that must dissolve a bridge (a rewrite before its segment, redaction, provenance normalization, merge unions, compaction) mark the covered versions with a sealed replay_inexact, and restore and get --at refuse them with history_version_unreconstructable. Equivalent independent repairs merge as equivalent_bridges, keeping both provenances. pm health names --append-only as the chain-mismatch remedy, including the bulk form.
Append-only history repair shipped in PR #1762

Add a case for equivalent_bridges to exhaustive switches over HistoryMergeStrategy; raw history readers should ignore the optional bridge and replay_inexact fields or verify through verifyHistoryChainWithVersion, and treat history_version_unreconstructable as a refused version

--append-only (SDK and MCP appendOnly) appends one sealed history_repair record whose bridge names each break and leaves every earlier line byte-identical. verifyHistoryChainWithVersion accepts a break only when the next bridge names it and reports bridged_segments. A rewrite that dissolves a bridge marks the covered versions with the sealed replay_inexact field, and restore and get --at refuse them with history_version_unreconstructable. The history merge driver adds the equivalent_bridges strategy, and pm health names --append-only as the remedy for history_drift_chain_mismatch

value.text:
Final bot round on the closeout head eff57588e: CodeRabbit 7 findings, Greptile 1. Seven were fixed in the following commit; the history-diff finding is already tracked on pm-vtg2d8.
- An equivalent-repair run followed by ordinary records on both sides (reciprocal merges that both kept working) was refused for contradictory order. The merge driver now normalizes the two runs into one shared run (ours plus neutral copies of theirs' repairs) before ordering the later records. This resolves the fourth case recorded on pm-vtg2d8.
- history-compact refuses a checkpoint inside a live bridged segment with history_compact_boundary_bridged and names the nearest boundaries; before, the rewrite failed verification untyped.
- A bridge naming an unsupported digest algorithm counts as unlocated instead of throwing, so redaction returns its typed refusal.
- Verbatim bridge preservation is off for continuous-surface rewrites and when the requested epoch differs from the segment's.
- The package closure check treats a dot-only specifier inside a loader call (require("./")) as a module reference and resolves a directory's package.json main.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 8 (gpt-6.2-sol, high, scoped to the commit after eff57588e): 9 findings, all fixed in the next commit.
- Packaging: the check had tested every candidate a reference could name. It now resolves each reference in Node's order: the exact file, CommonJS extensions, the directory's package.json main (itself resolved through extensions and an index), then the index. It does this once against the checkout and once against the packed set, and refuses when the checkout loads a module and the package does not load that same file. That one rule covers a packed sibling file taking precedence over a directory main, an extensionless main, a directory manifest left out of the package, and a root-level require("./"). Loader detection skips block and line comments between the call and the string.
- Merge: equivalent-repair normalization applies only when no repair of the runs recurs later and all four sides (both inputs and both rewritten sides) verify. Otherwise the streams merge as recorded, so an epoch-relabelled clone falls back to the union instead of returning an unverifiable fast-forward. When it applies, the equivalent-bridge path writes the normalized bytes instead of ours' original bytes. Receipts keep the original coordinates: the inputs' shared prefix, with theirs' neutral copies counted as theirs; a fast-forward of the rewritten sides reports equivalent_bridges.
- Rewrite preservation: a bridged segment counts as being on the requested epoch when its closer verifies under that epoch and every covered record declares it or inherits it by declaring none. A plain history-repair therefore keeps a segment holding an unversioned legacy record (negative control: the previous filter dissolves it).
- history-compact's bridged-boundary refusal names durable versions, including after an earlier compaction.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 9 (gpt-6.2-sol, high, scoped to 6ab9834ce) found 8 issues and Greptile found 2 on 0db4719f8. All are fixed in the next commit; one Greptile finding was already fixed in 6ab9834ce.
- Merge: normalization rebuilt both shared prefixes from ours, so a replay_inexact marker carried only by theirs on a shared record was lost (Greptile). Markers and bridges are now also collected from the recorded inputs. Negative control: without the fix the new case loses the marker. When normalization adds no neutral copy to ours, ours' original bytes (CRLF included) are kept.
- Rewrite preservation: each closer's verified epoch is recorded during the verification walk (module-private, so the public result shape is unchanged), not by re-verifying a growing prefix per bridge. Rewrites that re-anchor every record skip the check entirely.
- history-compact: on a legacy checkpoint without a trustworthy offset, a timestamp cutoff inside a bridged segment still refuses with history_compact_boundary_bridged, with timestamp guidance instead of history_version_mapping_unavailable.
- Package closure resolver: CommonJS appends only .js, .json and .node, so .cjs and .mjs load only by exact name. A terminal "/." or "/.." names a directory. An empty main is ignored. A main that resolves outside the package root or into node_modules is left to runtime staging. require() is judged by its literal spelling, an import by its URL spelling, any other string by both.
Declared scope of the resolver: relative quoted specifiers in staged JavaScript, resolved with Node's CommonJS file, main and index rules. It does not model package exports or imports maps, symlinks or custom loaders. The packed-runtime smoke, which installs the tarball and loads every SDK subpath, remains the end-to-end proof.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 10 (scoped to 38ad3bbeb, 6 findings) and CodeRabbit's full review of 38ad3bbeb (11 findings). Fixed in the next commit, except one CodeRabbit finding already tracked on pm-vtg2d8 (epoch-2 variant ambiguity).
- Merge: explicit replay_inexact markers come from both recorded inputs, while bridge coverage comes only from the normalized streams. Coverage from the recorded inputs had marked the repair that restored the state (negative control confirmed). A neutral copy keeps its original's identity after a later marker reseal: the alias searches every evidence entry, not only the newest.
- Redaction: a bridge located only because its covered records are already marked, without a digest match, now refuses with history_redact_bridge_unlocated (locateBridgedSegments reports it as undigested). Reads still use that location.
- Bridge digest: a key-preserving canonical JSON, so an own __proto__ key counts and key order does not.
- Append-only write: the readback loops to EOF, so a short read cannot report stream_changed for a committed bridge.
- pm health: --all --append-only is the bulk remedy only when every drifted stream has a chain mismatch. With other drift present, a chain mismatch keeps the per-item remedy. A test runs the advised remedies to a clean history_drift check in both cases. Doing that exposed a defect already on main: the missing-stream remedy cannot run. It is filed as pm-3os5p6.
- history-compact: legacy timestamp guidance uses the latest timestamp through the bridge.
- Package closure: escapes in a quoted specifier are decoded before resolution. require() also judges .json and .node targets. A main that leaves the packed first-party tree refuses (fail closed). A main's trailing slash is dropped as Node does. A string an expression transforms before loading is judged in both spellings.
- Docs: --append-only distinguishes a bridge from a reconciliation record and says a missing stream refuses. The chain-mismatch remedy says one record bridges every break in the stream.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 11 (scoped to 38ad3bbeb, 7 findings) and Greptile (1 finding, the same as the Codex compaction one). All fixed in the next commit.
- Bridge digest: the canonical JSON now orders keys exactly as stableStringify does, array-index keys first and numerically, then every other key by code unit. Records without an own __proto__ key therefore digest as before; a spec pins equality with stableStringify for integer-like keys.
- Package closure: the package side now resolves against the completed stage (first-party files plus the bundled runtime) instead of the first-party file list. A directory main into a staged production dependency passes, and one into a development-only dependency refuses. Loader detection skips comments between the loader name and its parenthesis. A transformed argument keeps its loader context, so require("./" + x) still names the directory. A block comment ends at its first "*/", so the pattern cannot span code or backtrack across adjacent comments; 40 adjacent comments scan in well under a second. Control-character escapes decode to their JavaScript values.
- history-compact: the latest timestamp through the bridge is a fold rather than a Math.max spread, so a long legacy stream keeps its timestamp guidance.
CodeRabbit's review of fe13525cc was rate limited; its previous full review is fully answered.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 12 (scoped to 2d733dd3e, 5 findings) and CodeRabbit's full review of 2d733dd3e (20 findings). The loop is not converging: each CodeRabbit pass over the whole diff raises 10 to 20 new edge cases. Following the bot-loop convergence rule, every Major and every quick correctness or documentation finding is fixed in the next commit. The rest are declined or deferred with reasons.
Fixed:
- Merge, both Majors: the equivalent-bridge output must verify before it is returned, otherwise the union handles it. A copy of a repair theirs marked keeps replay_inexact, because markers are collected over the complete output.
- Merge: a normalized merge that begins with every record ours recorded keeps ours' original bytes for that prefix, CRLF included. Malformed reanchor_evidence never aliases and never throws.
- Replay: only add and replace values are cloned. A copy or move onto its own path counts as effect-free, so it cannot claim a state change. A rewrite before a bridged segment that changes only an epoch label keeps the segment verbatim (negative control confirmed); an older test had encoded the dissolution.
- history_version_unreconstructable: the guidance distinguishes a live bridge from a marker left after dissolution.
- Append-only write: the path identity is checked before and after the readback.
- history-compact: when a timestamp through the bridge does not parse, only the earlier cutoff is offered.
- Package closure: the package side resolves against npm's final packlist, from a dry run of the stage, so a file npm omits from a bundled dependency counts as missing. Constant concatenations fold before resolution. A dot-only prefix of a dynamic expression names nothing. An import resolves as a URL against the importing module (whitespace, query, fragment and percent escapes per the URL parser). A manifest is read only when it is a regular file.
- Docs and completions: history_record_invalid is scoped to the shared decoder. The equivalent merge keeps ours byte-for-byte unless a marker must be propagated. The compaction refusal applies only while the bridge is live. stream_changed advises pm health before a retry. The salvage completions name null, boolean and number lines.
Declined or deferred:
- Keeping digests written by fe13525cc verifiable: only that unmerged intermediate commit wrote the other key order, and no release ever shipped it.
- Validating the planning snapshot's raw bytes for UTF-8: the apply refuses such bytes under the lock, so only a preview racing an out-of-band writer could differ.
- Bulk append-only advice when a chain mismatch is really patch_does_not_replay: heavy, recorded on pm-3os5p6.
- Epoch-2 variant ambiguity: already on pm-vtg2d8.

value.text:
Codex review round 13 (scoped to 2d733dd3e, 4 findings) and Greptile (1, the same as the first Codex finding). All fixed in the next commit; CodeRabbit's review of b007505b4 was rate limited.
- A copy onto its own path is effect-free only when the destination cannot be an array element; copying onto an index or "-" inserts a second element. A unit test pins the rule directly. Changing the break record's patch also changes its record hash, which masks the rule in a verifier-level case, so that weaker case was dropped.
- A rewrite that labels every record keeps a bridged segment verbatim only when its closer carries the declared epoch. An unlabelled closer is otherwise dissolved with its markers kept. Negative control: without the check, reanchoring the labelled legacy stream to epoch 1 fails with bridge_epoch_mismatch.
- Package closure: only complete string operands fold; a literal an expression transforms (".js".slice(3)) ends the fold, and the literal before it is judged as written. The dot-only exemption for non-loader strings also applies after a query or fragment, so new URL("./?view=modules", import.meta.url) is a directory read.
